<objective>
The tracer: one production-quality path from `fleet task create` all the way through to an archived
worktree and a recorded turn count, wired through every layer this phase will touch, verified
end-to-end against the fake-`claude` fixture.

Purpose: this phase spans worktree provisioning, process supervision, billing isolation, an in-process
queue, an HTTP surface, and a CLI. Proving that whole stack on one thin path first — on the executor's
best early-context tokens — catches an architectural dead end after one commit instead of after six
already-committed layers. Every later plan in this phase widens this slice rather than discovering it.

Output: a working `fleet task create` that provisions a locked worktree on a `fleet/<short-id>` branch,
spawns a billing-safe headless session with explicit caps, records `turns_used` from the terminal
`result` line, and archives the worktree while keeping the branch.
</objective>

  <action>
Wire ONE entry point through every layer to the far end of the stack. No batching, no second call site,
no alternative code path — but real error handling on this one path.

**`src/runner/runner.interface.ts`** — a small flat TypeScript `interface Runner` with exactly four
members per D-17: `provision(task)`, `spawn(task)`, `kill(task)`, `status(task)`. Match the project's
existing lightweight-interface style (`SpawnClaudeOptions`, `InspectRepoResult`, `ReadFleetYmlResult`) —
no class hierarchy, no abstract base. Export `ProvisionResult` (`{ worktreePath, branchName, baseRef }`),
`SpawnResult` (`{ exitCode, sessionId, turnsUsed, durationMs, terminalSubtype }`), and `RunnerStatus`
(`'idle' | 'provisioning' | 'running' | 'terminated'`). This is the RUN-07 seam: a future container
backend implements the same four members and populates `runner_meta`, requiring no schema change.

**`src/runner/worktree-manager.ts`** — the tracer needs only the create-and-lock half plus the
remove-and-keep-branch half. Follow `git-inspect.ts`'s convention exactly: every git invocation is
`execFileSync('git', [argv array], { cwd, stdio: 'pipe' })`, never a shell string, never string
interpolation. Define a `WorktreeError` class with a `code` field, mirroring `GitInspectError`'s shape,
with initial codes `worktree_locked`, `worktree_add_failed`, `base_ref_unresolvable`.

Export `worktreeRootFor(projectSlug, taskId)` returning
`join(resolveFleetHome(), 'worktrees', projectSlug, taskId)` — built only from the project's registered
slug and the server-generated task UUID, never from any request-body string. Export
`branchNameForTask(taskId)` returning `fleet/` plus `taskId.replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 8)`, and validate
that the input is a 36-character UUID before slicing, throwing `WorktreeError('invalid_task_id')`
otherwise — a short or empty short-id would produce an ambiguous or ref-illegal branch name.

Export `resolveBaseRef(repoPath, defaultBranch)` implementing D-18: if the repo has an `origin` remote,
run `git fetch origin` then return `refs/remotes/origin/<defaultBranch>`; otherwise return
`refs/heads/<defaultBranch>`. Export `ensureWorktree({ repoPath, projectSlug, taskId, defaultBranch })`
which for the tracer performs `git worktree prune`, then `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> <baseRef>`,
then `git worktree lock <path> --reason "fleet task <taskId>"`, and returns a `ProvisionResult`. The
`add -b <branch> <path> <baseRef>` form checks out ONLY the task branch, which is what makes SAFE-08
structural: the project's default branch is never the worktree's HEAD, and git independently refuses to
check out a branch already checked out elsewhere. Export `archiveWorktree({ repoPath, worktreePath })`
which runs `git worktree unlock <path>` then `git worktree remove <path>` and deliberately does NOT
delete the branch ref — the branch outliving the worktree is what makes the work inspectable afterward.
The full four-step idempotent algorithm, `.fleet.yml` setup commands, and dirty-work capture are plan
02-05's expansion; the tracer's `ensureWorktree` may assume a clean first run, and MUST NOT use
`--force` on removal.

**`src/runner/worktree-runner.ts`** — a `WorktreeRunner` class implementing `Runner`. Open the file with
a doc comment naming RUN-01/RUN-02/RUN-07/BILL-03/BILL-04 and the property it defends, matching
`env.ts`'s and `git-inspect.ts`'s header convention.

Export a pure `buildSpawnArgv(input)` function separate from the spawn itself, so the argv contract is
unit-testable without a process. It returns, in this order: `-p`, the task prompt, `--output-format`,
`stream-json`, `--verbose`, `--permission-mode`, `acceptEdits`, `--allowedTools`,
`Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep,Bash,TodoWrite,Task,WebSearch,WebFetch`, `--disallowedTools`,
`Bash(git push*),Bash(git remote*),Bash(sudo*)`, `--max-turns`, the resolved cap as `String(n)`,
`--model`, the resolved alias, `--setting-sources`, the empty string, `--settings`, and
`JSON.stringify(inlineSettings)`. Notes the executor must honor: the literal string `default` is NOT a
legal `--permission-mode` value on this CLI (SPIKE-02, observed) — omitting the flag is what "default"
means, so never emit that string. `--setting-sources` takes an empty-string argument, which
RESEARCH.md verified live on 2.1.218 returns exit 0 with `apiKeySource` preserved as `none` and
project-scope settings visibly excluded. Do NOT include `--include-hook-events` (deferred to Phase 3 by
D-15), and do NOT include the flag that disables discovery-and-keychain auth, which plan 02-02's
decision checkpoint prohibits outright.

Spawn with `spawn('claude', argv, { cwd: worktreePath, env: buildWorkerEnv({ ... }), detached: true, shell: false, stdio: ['ignore','pipe','pipe'] })`
from `node:child_process`. Use the built-in module — CONTEXT.md D-13 deliberately overrides the
`execa` entry in `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s stack table, because Fleet needs bespoke process-group kill
logic regardless and minimizing dependencies that shell out is itself a small security win. Do not
"correct" this back. `shell: false` plus an argv array plus never invoking a login shell is what
satisfies BILL-04. Persist `child.pid` into `tasks.runner_pid` and the ISO timestamp into
`tasks.runner_started_at` via the task service, and write `tasks.runner_kind` as `worktree`.

Parse stdout with `node:readline` over `child.stdout`, one `JSON.parse` per line inside try/catch. An
unparseable line is skipped, never thrown on. Capture `session_id` from the first line that carries it
and persist it to `tasks.session_id`. Capture `num_turns` from the terminal `result` line into
`turns_used`, and compute duration from `started_at`/`ended_at`. Do NOT persist `total_cost_usd` into any
task column — per D-29 it is an imputed API-equivalent price under subscription billing, not money that
left an account; if retained at all it belongs in the event payload under an explicitly imputed label.
Export `killTree(pid, grace)` sending `process.kill(-pid, 'SIGTERM')` against the whole process group,
with a `setTimeout` escalation to `SIGKILL` after the grace window, cleared on the child's `exit` event.
The negative-PID form signals every member of the group, which is what reaps grandchildren the agent's
own Bash tool calls spawn.

**`src/scheduler/queue.ts`** — the minimal `Scheduler` the tracer needs: a class wrapping
`new PQueue({ concurrency })` with `enqueue(taskId)` and a settable `concurrency`. `enqueue` records the
`DISPATCH` event through `recordEvent`, then calls `runner.provision()` and `runner.spawn()`, then
records the terminal event and calls `archiveWorktree()`. Pause, resume, kill switch, boot-time
reconstruction and rate-limit backoff are plan 02-09's expansion — the tracer implements dispatch only.
Follow `src/registry/projects.ts`'s typed-error-class convention: define `SchedulerError` with a `code`
field and add its codes to `CODE_TO_STATUS`.

**`src/tasks/service.ts`** — `createTask(db, input)` inserting a `tasks` row with `status: 'queued'`,
a `crypto.randomUUID()` id, and the resolved model and caps; and `getTask(db, id)` returning the row.
Throw a `TaskServiceError` with code `task_not_found` for an unknown id and `project_not_found` for an
unknown project. This module never issues `db.update(tasks).set({ status })` — status changes are
`recordEvent`'s exclusive job.

**`src/api/http/routes/tasks.ts`** — mirror `projects.ts` exactly: `app.withTypeProvider<ZodTypeProvider>()`,
a zod `createTaskBody` requiring `projectId` (or slug), `title`, and `prompt` and accepting optional
`model`, `maxTurns`, `wallClockCapMs`, and a `taskIdParams` schema of `z.object({ id: z.string().uuid() })`.
Register `POST /tasks` returning 201 with `{ task }`, and `GET /tasks/:id` returning `{ task }`. The body
schema must accept NO path component of any kind — the worktree path is derived server-side from the
registered project slug and the generated task UUID, which is what closes the path-traversal surface
RESEARCH.md's V12 note flags. Let `TaskServiceError`/`WorktreeError`/`SchedulerError` propagate to the
registered error handler; do not try/catch and render inline.

**`src/api/http/errors.ts`** — this is the ONLY plan in phase 02 that edits this file, so add the
COMPLETE set of codes every later plan in the phase needs, in one pass, and do not revisit it:
`task_not_found: 404`, `project_not_found: 404`, `project_archived: 409`, `invalid_task_id: 400`,
`worktree_add_failed: 500`, `worktree_locked: 409`, `worktree_dirty_capture_failed: 500`,
`worktree_path_outside_root: 500`, `branch_name_exhausted: 500`, `setup_command_failed: 500`,
`preflight_failed: 503`, `queue_paused: 409`, `task_not_running: 409`.
